# Copilot Instructions - Ada Tech Products Api Project

## 🌍 Language Rules

### Code and Documentation
- **ALL** code comments, documentation, commit messages, and technical content **MUST** be written in **English**
- **ALL** Markdown documentation files (.md) **MUST** be written in **English**
- Variable names, function names, class names: **English only**
- Log messages and error messages: **English only**
- API documentation and README files: **English only**
- Code documentation (XML comments, JSDoc, etc.): **English only**
- Documentation files in `docs/` folder: **English only**
- **NEVER** create .md files in Portuguese or any other language

### User-Facing Content
- User interface text, labels, and messages: Use **i18n/internationalization**
- Never hardcode user-facing strings in the code
- Always use translation keys from the i18n system

---

## 🔧 Backend Development Rules

### Code Style
- Use C# 14 features and .NET 10
- Follow Microsoft's C# coding conventions
- Use async/await for all I/O operations
- All public methods must have XML documentation comments in English

### Azure Functions
- Each function must have proper authorization levels
- Use dependency injection for services
- Follow the isolated worker model pattern
- All HTTP triggers should include proper error handling

### Database
- Use Entity Framework Core for all database operations
- Always use migrations for schema changes
- Include proper foreign key relationships
- Use appropriate indexes for performance

### DTOs and Mapping
- **ALWAYS** use Extension Methods for DTO mapping
- Location: `UserManagementBE/Extensions/Mapping/`
- Follow naming convention: `{EntityName}Extensions.cs`
- Methods should follow these patterns:
  - `ToResponseDto()` - Entity → Response DTO
  - `ToListDto()` - Entity → List/Summary DTO
  - `ToEntity()` - Create DTO → Entity
  - `UpdateFromDto()` - Update Entity from Update DTO

**Example:**
```csharp
// ❌ WRONG - Don't create DTOs inline
var response = new PolicyResponseDto
{
    Id = policy.Id,
    Name = policy.Name,
    // ... many more properties
};

// ✅ CORRECT - Use extension methods
var response = policy.ToResponseDto();
```

### Error Handling
- Use structured logging with proper log levels
- Return appropriate HTTP status codes
- Include meaningful error messages (in English)
- Never expose sensitive information in error responses

---

## 📁 Project Structure

### Backend Structure
```
AdaTech.Products.Api/
├── Data/              # DbContext and database configuration
├── Extensions/        # Extension methods (including Mapping)
├── Functions/         # Azure Functions (HTTP triggers)
├── Helpers/          # Utility classes
├── Middleware/       # Custom middleware
├── Migrations/       # EF Core migrations
├── Models/           # Domain entities
│   └── DTOs/        # Data Transfer Objects
└── Services/         # Business logic services
```
---

## 🔒 Security Rules

### Authentication & Authorization
- Implement proper CORS configuration
- Never store secrets in code (use Azure Key Vault or environment variables)

### Data Validation
- Validate all input on both frontend and backend
- Sanitize user input to prevent injection attacks
- Use TypeScript types for frontend validation
- Use Data Annotations for backend validation

---

## 📝 Documentation Rules

### Code Documentation
- All public APIs must have XML documentation (English)
- Include examples in documentation when helpful
- Document complex business logic with inline comments
- Keep documentation up to date with code changes

### Project Documentation
- **ALL** markdown files (.md) **MUST** be written in **English**
- Create/update markdown files in the `docs/` folder
- Use clear, descriptive file names (in English)
- Include code examples and screenshots when relevant
- Document all breaking changes
- **NEVER** create documentation in Portuguese or any other language
- Titles, headings, body text, code comments in docs: **English only**

---

### Database Migrations
- Always create migrations for schema changes
- Test migrations on development environment first
- Include rollback strategy in documentation
- Never modify existing migrations

---

## 📦 Dependencies

### Adding New Dependencies
- Evaluate necessity before adding new packages
- Check for security vulnerabilities
- Document why the dependency is needed
- Keep dependencies updated regularly

### Package Management
- Backend: Use NuGet packages
- Frontend: Use npm packages
- Lock dependency versions in production
- Review dependencies during code review

---

## 🎯 Best Practices

### Clean Code
- Follow SOLID principles
- Keep functions small and focused
- Use meaningful variable and function names (English)
- Avoid code duplication (DRY principle)
- Use extension methods for common operations

### Performance
- Use async/await for I/O operations
- Implement proper caching strategies
- Optimize database queries (use Include for eager loading)
- Minimize API calls from frontend

### Version Control
- Write clear commit messages (in English)
- Create feature branches for new work
- Keep commits atomic and focused
- Squash commits before merging to main

---

## 🔄 Refactoring Rules

### When to Refactor
- When adding new features that duplicate existing code
- When code becomes difficult to understand
- When performance issues are identified
- When test coverage is insufficient

### How to Refactor
- Write tests before refactoring
- Make incremental changes
- Test after each change
- Document breaking changes

---

## 📋 Code Review Checklist

Before submitting code for review, ensure:
- [ ] All text is in English (code, comments, docs)
- [ ] UI text uses i18n/translation keys
- [ ] Extension methods are used for DTO mapping
- [ ] No hardcoded strings in user-facing components
- [ ] Proper error handling is implemented
- [ ] Code follows project structure conventions
- [ ] Documentation is updated if needed
- [ ] No secrets or sensitive data in code
- [ ] Tests pass successfully
- [ ] Code builds without warnings

---

## 🆘 Getting Help

If you're unsure about any convention or pattern:
1. Check existing code for similar patterns
2. Review documentation in the `docs/` folder
3. Look for extension methods in `Extensions/Mapping/`
4. Check i18n translation files for frontend text patterns
5. Ask the team for clarification

---

**Remember:** These rules apply to ALL code contributions, regardless of when or by whom the code is written. Consistency is key to maintainability!
